court: In the High Court of Madras†
respondents: Managing Director Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Madurai) Ltd. and Others
advocates: For Respondents : Mr. S. Raja Standing Counsel for R 1 & R 2
Mr. S.C. Herold Singh Standing Counsel for R 3
prayer: PRAYER: Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, to issue a writ of mandamus directing the respondents to settle the belated payment interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on the delayed payment of retirement benefits, such as, provident fund Rs 19,13,235, gratuity Rs 16,85,446, leave salary Rs 7,85,808 and commutation Rs 9,96,358 from the date of retirement on 30-6-2025 till the date of settlement on 11-3-2026.
judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

Mummineni Sudheer Kumar, J.:— Mr S. Raja, learned Standing Counsel, takes notice for the respondents 1 & 2 and Mr S.C. Herold Singh, learned Standing Counsel, takes notice for the third respondent.

2. With the consent of both sides, this writ petition is disposed of at the admission stage.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Standing Counsels appearing for the respective respondents.

4. The learned counsel on either side unanimously agree that the issue involved in this writ petition is squarely covered by various Judgments passed by the Division Bench of this Court in W.A.(MD) No. 403 of 2010 and batch, dated 15-4-2014 and W.A.(MD) No. 1419 of 2021 and batch, dated 26-7-2021.

5. In the said circumstances, this writ petition is allowed and the respondents are directed to pay interest at the rate of 6% per annum for the belated payment of the petitioner's retirement benefits, such as, provident fund, gratuity, leave salary and commutation, from the date of his retirement till the date on which those benefits are paid to the petitioner. The respondents are further directed to comply with the said direction as expeditiously as possible, at any rate, within a period of five months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order. No costs.
